gist: China expelled a record 33 members from the Communist Party during its fifth plenum.
The gathering in Beijing saw record empty seats following extensive anti-corruption purges.
Analysts expect Xi Jinping to seek a fourth term at the 2027 Party Congress.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: China expelled 33 members from the Communist Party at the fifth plenum, a closed-door gathering in Beijing. Attendance fell to 279 members, marking the highest number of empty seats in modern Chinese history. High-ranking figures removed include former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui and top military figures Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The purges have gutted the Central Military Commission down to just two members, raising questions about military leadership and combat readiness. Observers note the campaign consolidates Xi Jinping's authority and targets disloyalty as he prepares for potential leadership changes.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The plenum laid groundwork for the next Party Congress in 2027, where analysts expect Xi to secure a fourth term. Xi will likely dominate personnel selections to fill the gaps left by the recent expulsions.

gist: A second fatal high-speed train collision in Spain has killed at least 69 people.
Leaked audio suggests computer and human errors caused the crash near Urda.
The disaster has intensified political pressure on Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez before elections.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A Renfe train rammed a stationary Iryo train from behind on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda, killing at least 69 people. The disaster follows a rail crash in January that killed 46 people. Leaked control-room audio suggested a computer failure and human error caused the collision.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The tragedy occurred a month before a snap general election, disrupting political campaigning across Spain. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his transport minister, Óscar Puente, face heavy criticism over rail safety. Conservative and far-right opposition parties have used the disaster to attack the government's management of public infrastructure.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Spain's main train drivers' union, Semaf, called a strike to demand that safety be prioritised over travel urgency. Opposition politicians are demanding accountability, while Vox has urged the Supreme Court to investigate Puente. Rail safety is expected to dominate the upcoming general election campaign.

quotes.text: The Spanish people need answers.
urgency to travel is never prioritised over safety

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Dónal Lunny, a prominent multi-instrumentalist, arranger and producer in Irish traditional music, died of cancer at the age of 79. He was known for playing the guitar, keyboards and bodhrán, and for popularising the Irish bouzouki. timeline.text: Manosphere and online misogyny should be treated as public health issues, say UK experts

gist: Experts argue online misogyny and the manosphere should be treated as public health issues.
A new report highlights how commercial models profit from extreme content and male grievances.
Experts stress addressing root causes and providing alternatives rather than just removing content.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Experts writing in the Lancet published a report calling for the government to treat the manosphere and online misogyny as public health issues. They describe the manosphere as a lucrative commercial ecosystem that profits from extreme misogyny and male grievance.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Young men facing loneliness, economic worries, and educational disengagement are vulnerable to online communities that blame feminism. Commercial models reward outrage, mirroring tactics used by the tobacco industry.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Experts recommend a coordinated response involving governments, schools, and health services, while offering boys credible alternatives for belonging and identity instead of simply removing harmful content.

To counter a lucrative online industry that profits from extreme misogyny by exploiting the isolation and insecurity of boys and young men.

The multi-billion dollar rail project has faced soaring costs and political challenges.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The chief executive of California’s high-speed rail authority, Ian Choudri, resigned abruptly on Wednesday. This followed a September investigative report from the state’s office of the inspector general that found the agency paid $543,000 in disallowed travel reimbursements for consultants, including money spent on gyms, an escape room and a nightclub. Choudri cited personal priorities in his resignation email, and Joe Stephenshaw was appointed as interim CEO.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The rail project has become a major financial and political headache for California. Eighteen years after voters approved it, no tracks have been laid, costs have soared above $100bn, and $4bn in federal funding was withdrawn last year. Potential gubernatorial candidates have also signaled that major staff changes are necessary to restore public confidence.

sections.text: Detectives in Scotland joined international efforts to target online gangs known as The Com. These groups groom and coerce vulnerable children, mostly young girls, into acts of self-harm and abuse on gaming platforms and social media. Police have identified victims and perpetrators in Scotland, with one arrest made so far.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts describe the networks as representing the gravest risk to children online. Abusers exploit young people for kudos or clout, escalating harm through manipulation and blackmail. While the scale is considered low-volume, the harm caused is extreme.

gist: US death row inmate Christa Pike released her first statement following a botched execution.
Pike reported experiencing continuous physical pain, mental suffering and medical complications after surviving.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused executions while an independent review investigates the failed procedure.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Christa Pike survived a failed lethal injection on 30 September in Tennessee. Execution staff spent nearly an hour attempting to establish an intravenous line to administer pentobarbital. Pike spent ten days in intensive care suffering from pneumonia, severe swelling and swallowing difficulties before returning to a rehabilitation centre infirmary. She subsequently released a statement describing constant physical pain, mental anguish and isolation, whilst criticising official incompetence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Pike is believed to be the only person to survive a lethal injection execution attempt. The botched procedure sparked widespread international shock. Slemmer's mother described the execution as a mess and demanded an apology, whilst the Tennessee Department of Correction defended its execution method.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused all executions for the rest of the year and ordered an independent review into the botched event. Lee indicated that Pike's death sentence will remain unchanged unless court rulings determine otherwise.

gist: Google booted up its Project Suncatcher satellite to run AI inference tasks in orbit.

Testing will evaluate how radiation and thermal stress affect chip performance in space.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Google successfully booted up its Project Suncatcher prototype satellite, which launched into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Using the onboard Gemma 4 model, the satellite generated its first response, a space-themed haiku, alongside telemetry prompts. The spacecraft carries four Tensor Processing Units, though power limits allow only one to operate at a time.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The project explores whether data centres can operate in space to process distributed AI workloads. Orbit exposes hardware to thermal stress and cosmic radiation, which can trigger bit flips in memory and corrupt data. Google aims to test whether inference workloads remain viable under these real-world conditions rather than ground simulations.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Google will test how the processors withstand orbital conditions before launching two interconnected satellites in 2027. Those future spacecraft will feature higher power generation and optical links.

fivew: Google conducted the experimental satellite test.

gist: Canada and the EU announced a new Alliance for the Future.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Canada and the European Union announced a new partnership called the Alliance for the Future during a two-day summit in Montreal. The alliance is open to like-minded countries and aims to offer stability, reduce trade and travel restrictions, and lead to an integrated market. Canada also agreed to contribute to a €90bn support loan for Ukraine and join Europe's supercomputing network.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The alliance serves as a hedge against unpredictable geopolitics, climate emergencies, and the weaponization of trade. It addresses concerns over reliance on American companies and defense technologies, while seeking to build certainty around supply chains and lower the cost of living for families.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Further discussions will lead to a more integrated market and new educational opportunities. A clearer scope regarding Canada's potential associate membership is expected to be decided at a 2027 summit.

quotes.text: Our societies have been shaken by new storms

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: According to the legend, Sawney Bean moved with a woman to a coastal cave in South Ayrshire. Their family grew to dozens, murdering and eating travellers on the highway between Girvan and Ballentrae. Eventually, King James and four hundred men hunted down the killers, who were captured, taken to Leith, and executed.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts suggest the story originated as sensationalised fan fiction during a time of anti-Scottish sentiment in England. Some historians believe the tale was created to degenerate Scots as barbaric. While experts like Dr Gordon McKelvie doubt Bean ever existed, locals like Chris Campbell argue the descriptions suggest he existed in Galloway, where myths may have protected smugglers.

Scotland, specifically associated with the South Ayrshire and Galloway coasts.

sections.text: The law has been used in hundreds of prosecutions since 2020 to smother public discussion about the monarchy. Courts interpret the law broadly, and defendants face severe sentences and difficulties mounting a defence.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Luigi Mangione's lawyers filed paperwork on Friday to dismiss his state-level case. This follows his federal guilty plea on 14 August to federal charges in the killing of UnitedHealthcare executive Brian Thompson. Mangione's lawyers argued that New York state's double jeopardy laws bar prosecution by the Manhattan district attorney. sections.heading: Why it matters

timeline.text: As Trump fans the flames of a world on fire, can diplomacy take back control?

gist: Trump and Israel launched a war on Iran, spreading conflict and global economic shocks.
The intervention strained US alliances, alienated Europe, and damaged Trump's domestic popularity.
Global powers and allies are increasingly questioning reliance on US security and technology.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Donald Trump and Israel launched a war on Iran in late February, triggering wider conflicts involving Hamas, Hezbollah, six Iranian militias, and the Houthis. The conflict disrupted global shipping and pushed worldwide inflation to 4%, while Saudi Arabia faced severe economic contractions and a ballooning budget deficit. Amid plunging poll numbers and rising fuel prices, Trump attempted to deflect blame toward Ukraine, demanding Volodymyr Zelenskyy stand down and restricting Ukrainian access to Starlink.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The interconnected nature of global conflicts means that US interventionism has sparked cascading crises, undermining stability in the Middle East and threatening peace worldwide. The resulting economic squeeze has alienated European leaders, who increasingly view US policies and tech monopolies as an existential threat to their sovereignty and political survival.

fivew: Donald Trump, regional leaders, and international diplomats.
US and Israeli military intervention in Iran sparked a widening chain of regional conflicts and global economic disruptions.
The Middle East, Ukraine, and various international diplomatic arenas.
Decades of geopolitical tensions and system failure culminated in military action that triggered unintended global consequences.

quotes.text: The fact now is that war anywhere threatens peace everywhere
There have, of course, been times in human history that were even darker and more terrible. But never, it seems, have there been times so despicable and, above all, so stupid.

sections.text: Basic, higher, and additional-rate tax rates on savings will rise to 24%, 44%, and 49%. Higher taxes make beating inflation on standard savings accounts harder, especially as personal savings allowances are quickly exceeded at current interest rates.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A study published in Science revealed that Manx shearwaters get jet-lagged when flying across time zones on foraging trips. Because they navigate using the Sun and their internal clocks fall out of sync with local time, they veer slightly off course.

timeline.text: UK police should not have let US force take over airbase trial, MoD documents show

gist: Cambridgeshire police wrongly let the US military investigate a fighter pilot, MoD documents show.
Capt Jacob Wulfson was tried on a US airbase rather than in English court.
A government inquiry is examining police handovers of serious crime investigations to the US.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Cambridgeshire police allowed US military police to take over the investigation of Capt Jacob Wulfson, an off-duty American fighter pilot accused of assaulting Sarah Steele. Wulfson was tried at a military tribunal on a US airbase in Suffolk rather than an English criminal court, where he was convicted of strangling an intimate partner and jailed for six months.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Ministry of Defence documents reveal officials believed the decision breached a long-established UK-US agreement. Under the agreement, UK police have primary jurisdiction over alleged crimes by Americans stationed in the UK unless committed while on duty or against military personnel.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The government has set up a cross-government inquiry to examine how police forces transfer serious crime investigations involving US military personnel to US military police.

quotes.text: this should absolutely have been for the UK courts

timeline.text: Starmer says UK must get closer to Europe as US relationship changes

gist: Keir Starmer urged the UK and Europe to build closer defence and security ties.
Starmer warned US relations have permanently shifted following Donald Trump's presidency.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham plans to seek closer EU agreements at an upcoming summit.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In his first major intervention since stepping down as prime minister, Keir Starmer told the British Irish Chamber of Commerce that the UK must be central to a stronger Europe. He warned that the US is now a less-reliable partner and will no longer bankroll European security.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Starmer stated that changes in Washington were permanent rather than an aberration, requiring Europe to take greater responsibility for its defence. He added that Brexit caused deep economic damage and advocated for closer economic and security cooperation.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: His successor, Andy Burnham, plans to be bolder regarding ties with the EU. Burnham will attend a UK-EU summit next month focusing on food standards, energy, and youth mobility, while also seeking a public debate on closer post-election ties.

fivew: Former UK prime minister Keir Starmer.
Former prime minister Keir Starmer called for the UK to draw closer to Europe on defence and security.
He delivered the remarks at the British Irish Chamber of Commerce after meetings in Dublin.
He argued that the US is a less-reliable partner and will no longer bankroll European security.

quotes.text: A stronger Europe is vital and the UK must be at the heart of it

timeline.text: England see off USA to return to winning ways

gist: England returned to winning ways with a victory over the United States in New Jersey.
Claudia Moloney-MacDonald scored four tries as England exploited space out wide.
The United States displayed impressive physicality and resistance throughout the contest.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England defeated the United States 55-12 in New Jersey during the WXV Global Series. Claudia Moloney-MacDonald scored four tries, while Jones, Venner, Field, Feaunati and Kabeya also crossed the line for England. Rogers and Zackary scored tries for the United States.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The performance leaves England head coach John Mitchell with plenty to ponder regarding set-piece solidity and attacking fluency before their Women's Six Nations title defence in April. Meanwhile, the United States demonstrated strong physicality and determination.

fivew: England defeated the United States in a rugby match.

gist: Lewis Hamilton believes he is unlike any driver Formula 1 has seen before.
The seven-time world champion intends to keep racing into his mid-forties.
Hamilton aims to fulfil a dream of racing at a new Grand Prix in Africa.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Lewis Hamilton stated at a news conference ahead of the Mexico Grand Prix that he is unlike any previous Formula 1 driver and plans to continue racing into his mid-forties.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Hamilton wants to fulfil a long-held ambition to race in Africa. Formula 1 has recently signed a ten-year agreement with Rwanda to host a race beginning in the early 2030s.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Hamilton remains fully committed to the sport for the foreseeable future, despite acknowledging potential age-related challenges ahead.

gist: Fleetwood Town will play either Everton or Newcastle United in the quarter-finals.
The League Two team advanced by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout.
The quarter-final matches are scheduled for the week starting 14 December.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Fleetwood Town advanced to the quarter-finals after overcoming Arsenal on penalties. They will now face the winners of the match between Everton and Newcastle United. Meanwhile, holders Manchester City were drawn against Bradford City, Liverpool will play Bournemouth, and Crystal Palace face Sunderland.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Fleetwood Town are the lowest-ranked club remaining in the tournament and have achieved a historic milestone by reaching the final eight.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Fleetwood await the conclusion of the fourth-round fixture between Everton and Newcastle to discover their specific opponent. The quarter-final ties are scheduled to occur during the week beginning 14 December.

fivew: Fleetwood Town reached the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.
The matches will take place in the week commencing 14 December.
